_comment: Shared search normalisation. Data, not code, so the browser (JS) and the build pipeline (Python) can both read this one file instead of each keeping a copy. Change it here and both sides change together.
_rules: Fold full-width U+FF01-U+FF5E to their half-width twins, so a half-width query reaches names like 鲁格 AC556（刺刀）.
Map CJK Roman numeral characters to digits, so 3 finds Ⅲ型防弹背心.
Map standalone multi-letter ASCII Roman numerals to digits, so 3 also finds 'Vest, type III'.
Remove all whitespace, so 鲁格AC556 finds 鲁格 AC556.
_cjkNumeralsNote: Both cases are listed on purpose. U+2160-U+2169 (Ⅰ…) and U+2170-U+2179 (ⅰ…) are distinct characters, and BOTH JavaScript's toLowerCase() and Python's str.lower() map the former to the latter. A table that only held one case would stop matching depending on where the fold ran — which is exactly the bug this file exists to prevent. Listing both makes the order of operations irrelevant.
_asciiNumeralsNote: Single-letter forms (i, v, x) are deliberately absent: in this catalog they are far more likely to be real tokens than numbers, and folding them matches things nobody asked for.
